title: Technical Product Manager - Gateway
description: Valor PayTech fosters a vibrant and nurturing work atmosphere that motivates employees to innovate and excel. The culture is deeply rooted in collaboration and ongoing development, offering team members abundant opportunities for professional advancement and skill improvement. Emphasizing innovation excellence and cultural expansion, the company greatly values the diversity of its workforce, believing it to be a cornerstone of its success. Role Overview Valor PayTech is hiring a Technical Product Manager to own the internal software development lifecycle for our Valor Gateway and Portal — the system of record that powers the entire Credit card processing, Payment Gateway, POS Terminals, SWITCH processing, ECOM Channel, Virtual terminal including ACH capability, and ISVs support. This is a hands-on, in-the-weeds role for someone who thrives at the intersection of product, process, and engineering execution. You will report directly to the Senior Technical Product Manager and act as the operational and technical backbone of the Gateway’s roadmap — translating business priorities into clear, complete engineering requirements, managing sprint execution, and ensuring releases are delivered with quality and on schedule. Above all, this role owns the discipline of getting analysis right the first time : before a change reaches engineering, you are accountable for enumerating its full impact across the platform, so that what we build is consistent, complete, and free of the gaps that surface late in production. This role does not require coding ability, but candidates with hands-on technical fluency (SQL, scripting, API / data literacy) will be considered a strong asset given the complexity of the systems involved. What We’re Looking For Four qualities define success in this role: A Self-Starter and Owner — You take end-to-end ownership of your platform’s SDLC without waiting to be directed. You drive backlog, analysis, and releases forward, chase down open questions across teams, and treat every gap between intent and delivery as yours to close. Technically Fluent — You are comfortable in the details of a complex payments platform — transaction flows, data models, integrations, and configuration — and can hold a credible technical conversation with engineers and QA. You reason about systems, not just features. Rigorous and Complete — You do not stop at the happy path. Before a change is committed, you systematically map its full impact surface — every transaction type, user persona, device population, credential form, processing feature, integration rail, and configuration state it could touch — so nothing is silently left behind. Completeness of analysis is the single most important thing this role protects. A Strong Executor and Communicator — You run disciplined agile ceremonies, write specifications engineering can build against without guessing, and communicate clearly with a US-based team — turning business and compliance needs into precise, unambiguous requirements. What You’ll Own SDLC Ownership and Delivery End-to-end SDLC management for Valor Gateway and Portal — backlog grooming, sprint planning, release coordination, and go-live sign-off, working closely with engineering leads and QA. Project estimation and resource planning, partnering with the Senior Technical Product Manager on scoping, prioritization, and developer-day forecasting. Release documentation, including change logs, workflow enhancement specs, and cross-processor integration notes. Own phase one of the SDLC — analysis and requirements gathering — as the point where quality is decided. For every change, enumerate the complete impact surface before engineering commits. Facilitate pre-commitment reviews with engineering and QA — a shared walkthrough of scope and impact before build begins. Translate business and compliance requirements into detailed technical specifications, user stories, and acceptance criteria that engineering can execute against without ambiguity. Platform Domain: Valor Payment Gateway and ISV Project Understanding Valor Payment Gateway capabilities and work towards offering them for the ISVs Handling ISVs requirements, lining up for work Prioritize based on the feasibility and the market value What You’ll Bring 7+ years of experience in technical product management, product ownership, or a closely related role, ideally within fintech, payments, banking, or merchant services. Proven experience managing a software development lifecycle: writing requirements, grooming backlogs, running agile ceremonies, and coordinating releases with engineering teams. Demonstrated rigor in requirements analysis — a track record of thinking through the full scope of a change and its edge cases up front, rather than discovering them after release. Strong analytical and process-design skills, with comfort interpreting data to monitor transactional and non-transactional activity. High proficiency in written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate effectively with a US-based team and accurately translate their business requirements into clear PRDs and project plans. Demonstrated comfort using AI tools (e.g., for documentation, analysis, or workflow automation) as part of regular product management practice. A collaborative work style and willingness to work a hybrid schedule from Valor PayTech’s Chennai office. Experience reporting to or partnering closely with a Product Owner in a structured product organization. Nice to Have (Strong Bonus) US Payment Knowledge, credit card processing and working on ISV products POS machines development, APP building, API integration Web Apps development and payment integration Familiarity with payments infrastructure and terminology — processors (such as TSYS, Fiserv), ACH / NACHA, ISO 8583, PCI DSS — gained through hands-on product or technical work. Big plus – but not required. Working knowledge of SQL for querying transaction, settlement, or merchant data. Scripting ability (e.g., Python) to support data analysis, automation, or reporting tasks. Exposure to REST APIs, JSON / XML data structures, or systems integration concepts. Prior experience with risk / fraud monitoring tools or chargeback and dispute workflows. Certifications such as CSPO, PMI-ACP, or processor-specific training (e.g., TSYS University). Why Join Valor PayTech You’ll take ownership of a mission-critical platform that touches every stage of the Valor payment gateway and ISV relationship, working alongside a focused product and engineering team in our Chennai office. This is an opportunity to shape how a fast-growing Payment gateway integrating with ISVs to utilize our feature — and to set the standard for how analysis and requirements are done — with direct visibility into the Product and broader leadership team.

description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright · TypeScript · pytest · Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · SQL · REST · OpenAPI · GitHub Actions · Docker · HL7 v2 · FHIR · ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language , enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team Good to have as well Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence Testing integrations with devices or external systems — an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed Security testing basics — role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten — and reading a VAPT report What You'll Bring Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work Methodical about the awkward cases — the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice — because those are where a hospital gets hurt Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover

the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language, enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; title: Infrastructure Specialist
description: Who We Are At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Your role Step into the engine room of enterprise technology, where every decision you make can shape how a customer’s systems perform today - and scale for tomorrow. You’ll dive deep into complex infrastructure environments, solving challenging technical problems, designing seamless integrations and ensuring systems run reliably at every level. Your expertise across networks, endpoints and mainframes, paired with a knack for logical problem-solving and clear documentation, will guide projects from concept to execution. Your solutions will make a real impact that customers notice and remember. In this role, you’ll balance hands-on delivery with long-term strategic planning. From analyzing issues and testing solutions to automating processes and integrating across platforms, your work will touch every layer of IT infrastructure. You’ll collaborate with Architects, Technicians and Project Managers, gaining broad exposure and continuous opportunities to grow your skills and influence. What you will do Analyze and Solve •Diagnose complex issues across servers, networks, cloud environments and systems to identify root causes •Recommend solutions that balance technical feasibility, timelines and customer priorities •Test, refine and automate processes to improve reliability, efficiency and repeatability •Assess risks proactively and implement strategies to prevent disruptions Design and Integrate •Plan end-to-end infrastructure solutions across platforms and technologies •Integrate systems in hybrid cloud and on-prem environments to ensure seamless operation •Automate workflows and processes to streamline delivery and reduce errors •Document architectures and procedures for hand-offs, knowledge sharing and operational continuity Collaborate and Deliver •Coordinate cross-functional teams including Architects, Project Managers and Technicians •Drive project delivery from initiation to completion with attention to quality and timelines •Communicate technical solutions clearly to customers and stakeholders •Build customer confidence by delivering tangible, high-impact results Grow and Advance •Expand technical expertise across cloud platforms, enterprise IT systems and emerging technologies •Earn certifications and qualifications while applying them on real projects •Pursue career paths toward Architect or Distinguished Engineer roles Who You Are Required skills and experience •Deep expertise within specific technology domain areas (e.g., software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics) •Enterprise IT application experience •Hands-on experience in at least one of the following: software development, DevOps engineering, systems administration, or systems architecture in public cloud AWS domain •In-depth knowledge of Windows and Linux Operating System Preferred skills and experience •Familiar with a variety of IT concepts, practices, and procedures •Knowledge of design techniques, tools, and principals involved in production of precision technical plans, blueprints, drawings, and models •Logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems •Analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail Being You The “Kyn” in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way. What You Can Expect Your career with us isn’t just a job—it’s an adventure with purpose. We offer a dynamic, hybrid-friendly culture that supports your well-being and empowers you to grow. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health—because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best. From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth. We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what’s next. Get Referred! If you know someone that works at Kyndryl, when asked ‘How Did You Hear About Us’ during the application process, select ‘Employee Referral’ and enter your contact's Kyndryl email address.

title: Senior Network Engineer (Voice & IPX)
description: Employment Type Permanent Closing Date 12 Nov 2026 11:59pm Job Title Senior Network Engineer (Voice & IPX) Job Summary Job Description As a Senior Network Engineer (Voice & IPX) , you’ll help shape the future of Telstra’s international mobility, voice, and interconnect capabilities. This individual contributor role is responsible for ensuring Telstra’s international network delivers a reliable, high-quality experience for interconnect and roaming partners, suppliers, and customers. You’ll contribute to the analysis, architecture, design, development, deployment, and optimisation of network technologies, with a strong focus on interoperability across multiple network domains. You’ll drive technology evolution across Telstra’s International Core Voice, IPX, and Mobility/Roaming platforms, delivering scalable and resilient solutions supporting international voice, mobility and roaming services, signalling platforms, and specialised international network services. Your focus will span the infrastructure, virtualisation, orchestration, application, IP network, and security layers, including: Oracle DSR, Ribbon SBC and PSX, and A2P SMS applications Cisco and Juniper switching and routing Check Point firewalls and network security NFV, cloud-native architectures, orchestration, and automation You’ll provide technical leadership in delivering innovative, next-generation network solutions that improve service quality, operational efficiency, resilience, and Telstra’s position in the global mobility and interconnect landscape. What We Offer Performance-related pay Access to thousands of learning programs so you can level-up Global presence across 22 countries; opportunities to work where we do business. Purchased annual leave scheme Additional Telstra day off Additional 30% off Telstra products and services Toolkit provided (laptop + mobile phone + plan paid for) What You’ll do Design, develop, deploy, and optimise solutions across International Voice, IPX, Mobility, and Roaming networks. Drive network transformation through NFV, cloud adoption, automation, and software-defined networking. Deliver secure, scalable, high-performing interconnect and roaming solutions. Provide specialist expertise across signalling, voice, IPX, roaming, and interconnect, ensuring integration with adjacent network technologies. Support Cisco and Juniper switching and routing infrastructure across the International Voice and IPX networks. Manage Check Point firewalls and network security controls, ensuring compliance with Telstra security policies and standards. Manage deployment, configuration, and lifecycle of Oracle DSR, Ribbon SBC and PSX, and A2P SMS platforms. Manage and support the infrastructure, virtualisation, and orchestration layers hosting International platforms and applications. Collaborate with internal stakeholders, international partners, customers, and vendors to deliver strategic network capabilities. Lead troubleshooting and resolution of complex network issues to maintain service availability and customer experience. Manage hardware and software currency, security patching, resiliency assessments, and sustainability requirements. Produce and review High Level Designs, test plans, and Methods of Procedure, and execute changes under Telstra change governance. Contribute to network strategy, technology roadmaps, architecture standards, and continuous improvement. Your Technical Expertise You’ll bring strong knowledge and experience across: Voice & IPX: Softswitches, Ribbon SBC, Ribbon PSX, Media Gateways, Oracle DSR, Oracle/Tekelec EAGLE STP, DNS/ENUM, A2P SMS Protocols: VoIP, SIP, TDM, IPX, Diameter, SS7/SIGTRAN, LTE, 3G/4G/5G, VoLTE/IMS IP & Security: Cisco and Juniper switching/routing, IP/MPLS, VLAN/VRF, BGP/OSPF, Check Point firewalls, network segmentation, signalling and interconnect security Virtualisation & Orchestration: Red Hat Virtualisation, NFV/VNF/CNF, cloud-native platforms, orchestration and automation tooling Network Domains: International Core Voice & IPX, Voice & IPX Signalling, Mobility & Roaming, Wholesale Voice, OTT Voice Monitoring & Assurance: Traffic Management Systems, Real-Time Traffic Monitoring, Genview Analytics, Performance Intelligence Centre, Splunk, Grafana, Inventory Management Lifecycle Management: Hardware and Software Currency, Security Patching, Resiliency and Sustainability Concepts and Management About You Bachelor’s degree in Telecommunications Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant technical qualifications. Minimum 8 years’ relevant experience in voice, signalling, IPX, and/or mobility/roaming network engineering. Strong understanding of international Voice, IPX, Mobility/Roaming, and carrier interconnect requirements. Hands-on experience with Oracle DSR, Ribbon SBC and PSX, and A2P SMS platforms, including deployment and management. Experience configuring and supporting Cisco and Juniper switches and routers in carrier-grade environments. Experience managing Check Point firewalls and network security controls. Sound knowledge of virtualisation, NFV, cloud-native architectures, and orchestration platforms. Sound understanding of SIP, Diameter, SS7/SIGTRAN, and IP networking protocols. Experience as a technical lead on medium to large engineering projects, preferably across voice or mobility networks. Ability to review technical solutions, conduct impact analysis, and plan controlled implementations. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and root-cause analysis skills. Excellent interpersonal, vendor, and stakeholder management skills. Certifications such as CCNP, JNCIP, Check Point CCSA/CCSE, or Red Hat will be highly regarded. Who You’ll Work With Internally, you’ll work closely with: IP, Transmission, Security, and Network Optimisation teams Voice Network Operations groups (TGOC) and Major Incident Management Product, Architecture, and Cloud/Virtualisation Infrastructure teams Network Resilience, Change Management, and Cyber Security teams Finance teams Externally, you’ll coordinate and deliver programs under the International Voice and IPX Engineering program of works, partnering with international interconnect and roaming partners, IPX carriers, customers, and technology vendors including Oracle, Ribbon, Cisco, Juniper, and Check Point. Why Join This Team? You’ll work at the heart of Telstra’s international network, combining carrier-grade telecommunications expertise with NFV, cloud-native networking, automation, orchestration, and next-generation network technologies. It’s an opportunity to influence the evolution of Telstra’s international Voice, IPX, signalling, mobility, roaming, IP, security, and virtualisation environments while working with global partners and leading technology vendors. Diversity is more than a policy – it’s how we thrive We know diverse teams deliver better outcomes, and we’re committed to creating an environment where everyone feels safe, respected, and supported — regardless of gender, background, or ability. We strongly encourage women and gender-diverse people to apply and are happy to discuss flexible working arrangements or adjustments to the recruitment process.

title: Software Engineer
description: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The LS-SWIFT division delivers high-throughput patterned wafer inspection systems that support advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its mission is to provide industry-leading defect detection with optimal cost of ownership across a wide range of applications. LS systems enable precise, cost-effective inspection for cutting-edge process nodes, while SWIFT systems offer comprehensive macro inspection of all wafer surfaces—capabilities that are especially critical for advanced packaging, as well as logic, memory, and automotive applications. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. Company Overview KLA is a global leader in diversified electronics for the semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem. Virtually every electronic device in the world is produced using our technologies. No laptop, smartphone, wearable device, voice-controlled gadget, flexible screen, VR device or smart car would have made it into your hands without us. KLA invents systems and solutions for the manufacturing of wafers and reticles, integrated circuits, packaging, printed circuit boards and flat panel displays. The innovative ideas and devices that are advancing humanity all begin with inspiration, research and development. KLA focuses more than average on innovation and we invest 15% of sales back into R&D. Our expert teams of physicists, engineers, data scientists and problem-solvers work together with the world’s leading technology providers to accelerate the delivery of tomorrow’s electronic devices. Life here is exciting and our teams thrive on tackling really hard problems. There is never a dull moment with us. Group/Division With over 40 years of semiconductor process control experience, chipmakers around the globe rely on KLA to ensure that their fabs ramp next-generation devices to volume production quickly and cost-effectively. Enabling the movement towards advanced chip design, KLA's Global Products Group (GPG), which is responsible for creating all of KLA’s metrology and inspection products, is looking for the best and the brightest research scientist, software engineers, application development engineers, and senior product technology process engineers. The LS-SWIFT Division of KLA’s Global Products Group provides patterned wafer inspection systems for high-volume semiconductor manufacturing. Its mission is to deliver market-leading cost of ownership in defect detection for a broad range of applications in the production of semiconductors. Customers from the foundry, logic, memory, automotive, MEMS, advanced packaging and other markets rely upon high-sample wafer inspection information generated by LS-SWIFT products. LS (Laser Scanning) systems enable cost-effective patterned wafer defect detection for the industry’s most sophisticated process technologies deployed in leading-edge foundry, logic, DRAM, and NAND fabs. SWIFT (Simultaneous Wafer Inspection at Fast Throughput) systems deliver all-wafer-surface (frontside, backside, and edge) macro inspection that is critical for automotive IC, MEMS, and advanced packaging processes as well as foundry/logic and memory fabs. LS-SWIFT operates from a global footprint that includes the US, Singapore, India and Germany, and serves a worldwide customer base across Asia, Europe and North America. Design skills is a plus. Good analytical and problem-solving abilities Thorough knowledge of SDLC and software engineering Strong verbal and written communication and team-work skills Ability to develop Software with Clean Code and SOLID principles Minimum Qualifications Master's Level Degree Bachelor's Level Degree and related work experience of 2+years Minimum Qualifications Master's Level Degree or work experience of 0 years , Bachelor's Level Degree or work experience of 1 years About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. Use of AI Statement At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset. We offer a competitive, family friendly total rewards package. title: Junior Data Scientists
description: Job Requirements Role: To contribute to the end-to-end development and product lifecycle management of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) systems as part of an R&D organization. The Junior Data Scientist supports the definition of intended algorithm performance, the development and curation of representative data and annotations, the development of AI/ML algorithms, and the generation of scientific evidence demonstrating stand-alone algorithm performance. The candidate is expected to: Apply scientific, statistical, machine learning, and software engineering methods to develop and evaluate AI/ML algorithm components for defined product use cases. Work with experienced Data Scientists, product management, clinical or domain experts, software developers, and quality and regulatory functions to translate customer needs and the intended use into measurable algorithm performance targets. Support the definition, sourcing, curation, documentation, and maintenance of representative data cohorts and annotations required for training, tuning, and evaluation. Plan and execute reproducible scientific evaluations that provide objective evidence of algorithm performance, limitations, and suitability for the intended use. Contribute the Data Science work products and evidence required for integration of AI/ML algorithm components into products and for their verification, validation, regulatory release, and lifecycle monitoring. What are my responsibilities? As a Junior Data Scientist, you are required to: Support the finalization of product and algorithm concepts by translating customer needs, intended use, clinical or technical requirements, and applicable regulatory considerations into measurable state-of-the-art performance targets. Contribute to the definition of the AI/ML development and scientific evaluation strategy for assigned algorithm components under the guidance of experienced Data Scientists. Perform exploratory data analysis and data risk assessments to identify data gaps, quality issues, potential bias, confounding factors, outliers, and limitations that may affect algorithm development or evaluation. Define and document data needs for training, tuning, and evaluation, including relevant subgroups and acceptance criteria, so that data cohorts are representative of the intended use and aligned with the product and regulatory strategy. Support the specification of annotations, acceptance criteria, and quality controls; collaborate with qualified internal or external suppliers on sourcing data and annotations. Curate, version, maintain, and document representative data cohorts and ensure data provenance, traceability, quality, and fitness for purpose together with data management stakeholders. Design, implement, train, tune, and technically characterize AI/ML algorithm components using appropriate machine learning, deep learning, statistical, or generative AI methods. Define scientifically justified metrics, evaluation methods, test cases, and acceptance criteria to assess stand-alone algorithm performance, including relevant aspects such as accuracy, robustness, reliability, generalizability, explainability, bias, and subgroup performance. Implement and execute reproducible bench tests on representative evaluation cohorts and relevant subgroups as part of the verification and validation strategy. Analyze and interpret evaluation results, investigate failure modes, document residual limitations, and derive evidence-based recommendations for algorithm improvement and product decisions. Document development and evaluation activities and contribute to Data Science work products such as data management information, annotation specifications, scientific evaluation test cases, and scientific evaluation reports. Provide scientific evidence and technical input for product reviews and regulatory submissions and support responses to questions concerning data, annotations, evaluation methods, and stand-alone algorithm performance. Support the design and execution of clinical investigations, reader studies, or other studies when additional evidence is required by the product or regulatory strategy. Collaborate with software engineering and MLOps functions to establish reproducible pipelines, versioned artifacts, automated tests, controlled deployment, and integration of algorithm components into the product. Help define and implement monitoring metrics for detecting data anomalies, outliers, and algorithm performance drift across the product lifecycle. Regularly review advances in Data Science and AI and assess their applicability to the development and evaluation of AI/ML products. Qualification: Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Medical Informatics, or a related quantitative or engineering field. A Ph.D. is welcome but not required. The candidate should have completed university-level coursework or equivalent practical training in: Probability, statistics, and experimental design Artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning Linear algebra, optimization, and numerical methods Data structures, algorithms, and software programming Model evaluation, scientific methodology, and interpretation of empirical results Experience level: This is a junior R&D position. Relevant experience may have been gained through academic research, a thesis, internships, working-student assignments, or up to approximately three years of professional work in Data Science, machine learning, AI research, or AI/ML product development. Demonstrated hands-on experience in developing and scientifically evaluating AI/ML models is more important than a specific number of years. Desired Knowledge & Experience: Sound understanding of machine learning, deep learning, statistical analysis, experimental design, and model evaluation. Active programming skills in Python and practical experience with libraries and frameworks such as NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Keras. Hands-on experience with the development workflow of AI/ML models, including data preparation, training, tuning, evaluation, error analysis, reproducibility, and documentation. Ability to define meaningful performance metrics, evaluation cohorts, subgroup analyses, test methods, and acceptance criteria for the intended use of an AI/ML algorithm. Understanding of data quality, representativeness, bias, annotation quality, data provenance, and traceability in AI/ML development. Knowledge of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) concepts and tooling, including source and data versioning, reproducible pipelines, experiment tracking, automated testing, CI/CD, deployment, and monitoring. Hands-on exposure to current Large Language Models and Generative AI, including foundation models, prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and model adaptation or fine-tuning. Knowledge of Agentic AI, including tool-using models, multi-step workflows, orchestration, memory, and autonomous or semi-autonomous decision paths, is an advantage. Experience or strong interest in the systematic evaluation of LLM, Generative AI, and Agentic AI systems, including task-specific benchmarks, groundedness and factuality, robustness, reproducibility, human evaluation, safety and guardrail testing, tool-use correctness, and analysis of failure modes. Experience with databases and query languages such as SQL; knowledge of Kusto Query Language, Snowflake, or graph databases such as Neo4j is an advantage. Exposure to cloud-based data and AI environments, preferably Microsoft Azure, such as Azure Blob Storage, Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Azure Machine Learning, Azure Monitor, or Azure DevOps. Experience with structured and unstructured data, for example machine logs, event data, Parquet files, text data, or multimodal data. Knowledge of healthcare, medical technology, clinical data, or interoperability standards such as DICOM is preferred. Basic project management skills and familiarity with working in cross-functional R&D or product-development teams. Required Soft Skills & Other Capabilities: Scientific mindset, strong analytical ability, and attention to detail. Commitment to objective evidence, reproducibility, traceability, data integrity, and responsible AI development. Curiosity and resilience to investigate unexpected results, challenge assumptions, and improve models based on evidence. Collaborative approach to working with Data Scientists, domain experts, software engineers, product management, and quality and regulatory stakeholders. Ability to work independently within an agreed scope and to seek guidance when technical, scientific, product, or regulatory implications require alignment. Clear written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to explain methods, results, uncertainties, limitations, and risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

title: Software Development Engineer, DSP Tech
description: DESCRIPTION Do you want to be part of the team that transforms how safety decisions are made for Amazon's Delivery Service Partners (DSPs) across 21 countries? Are you passionate about building intelligent, data driven platforms that protect delivery associates every single day? DSP SafetyTech is a newly formed team serving as the intelligence layer between safety signals and decisions — interpreting what happened, routing it to who can act, and ensuring no safety event goes unresolved. Today, safety data is fragmented across seven systems with no single technical owner, causing attribution errors, reconciliation gaps, and duplicated logic. We're changing that. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build a governed safety intelligence platform. You will contribute to three critical pillars: Safety Data as a Service (SDaaS), a governed serving layer consolidating telematics, incidents, and contextual enrichment; DSP Facing Mechanisms, a unified configuration layer managing compound signals and business rules across DSP facing surfaces; and Advanced Analytics and Agentic Capabilities, predictive models and AI agents that provide actionable safety insights. This is a rare opportunity to join a team building a platform from the ground up that will directly impact the safety of delivery associates worldwide. Key job responsibilities Design, develop, test, and deploy software components for a governed data serving platform that consolidates telematics, incident reports, video evidence, and contextual enrichment from multiple upstream systems Build and maintain backend services and APIs that support a unified configuration layer where safety business rules are authored, validated, versioned, and distributed Develop frontend components for a consolidated safety dashboard, a single view where signals, scorecard outcomes, alerts, event video, and interventions come together • Implement compound safety signals that combine individual data sources into higher order, actionable safety indicators • Write clean, maintainable, and well tested code following software engineering best practices Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and operational excellence activities Collaborate with data engineers and data scientists to integrate data pipelines and model outputs into production services Contribute to automated evidence preservation mechanisms to address short video retention windows Troubleshoot and resolve production issues, participating in on call rotations to ensure system reliability Work with cross functional teams including product managers, stakeholders across investigations, claims, insurance, and accountability to understand requirements and deliver solutions A day in the life You will be part of a team building the safety intelligence backbone for Amazon's DSP ecosystem. Your day may involve writing and reviewing code for backend services, building frontend features for the safety dashboard, discussing design approaches with your team, or debugging a production issue. You will collaborate closely with data engineers and data scientists to bring data driven capabilities to life. You'll participate in sprint planning, stand ups, and retrospectives, contributing ideas to improve both the product and the development process. You will have the opportunity to learn and grow across the full stack, from data pipelines to user facing experiences, while working on a platform that scales across multiple countries. About the team DSP Safety Tech is a newly established team with a clear mission: convert every safety event into a clear, trusted action for every DSP, in every market, every time. Our North Star is ensuring every safety signal reaches the people who can act on it, with the context needed to make timely decisions, so risks are identified earlier, decisions are made consistently, and every Delivery Associate goes home safely. We operate at the intersection of data engineering, applied science, and product development, serving stakeholders from investigators to insurance to DSP owners themselves. We're building from the ground up with a strong vision, executive sponsorship, and the freedom to innovate across the full stack, from governed data pipelines to AI powered agentic experiences. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build a governed safety intelligence platform. You will contribute to three critical pillars: Safety Data as a Service (SDaaS), a governed serving layer consolidating telematics, incidents, and contextual enrichment; DSP Facing Mechanisms, a unified configuration layer managing compound signals and business rules across DSP facing surfaces; and Advanced Analytics and Agentic Capabilities, predictive models and AI agents that provide actionable safety insights. This is a rare opportunity to join a team building a platform from the ground up that will directly impact the safety of delivery associates worldwide. You will collaborate closely with data engineers and data scientists to bring data driven capabilities to life. You will have the opportunity to learn and grow across the full stack, from data pipelines to user facing experiences, while working on a platform that scales across multiple countries. title: Quality Control Engineer
description: 1. Inward Quality Control (QC): Inspect and evaluate raw materials, components, and products received from vendors to ensure they meet company specifications and quality standards. Conduct thorough testing and analysis of incoming materials to identify defects, inconsistencies, or deviations from quality requirements. Document findings from inward quality inspections and coordinate with the procurement team to resolve any quality issues with suppliers. Maintain a record of inspection results and report any non-conformance to management for corrective actions. 2. Quality Alerts and Communication: Issue quality alerts when defects or quality issues are identified during the inspection process. Ensure that quality alerts are communicated promptly to the relevant teams, including production, procurement, and vendors. Follow up on the implementation of corrective measures resulting from quality alerts and ensure timely resolution of identified issues. Maintain a log of quality alerts to track recurring issues and their resolution status. 3. Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA): Implement corrective actions for any identified non-conformance or quality issues, ensuring that root causes are effectively addressed. Develop and monitor preventive actions to avoid the recurrence of similar issues, ensuring long-term improvements in the quality system. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to investigate the causes of quality defects and implement solutions that align with company goals. Document all corrective and preventive actions taken and evaluate their effectiveness over time. 4. In-Process Quality Control (IP QC): Monitor and control quality throughout the production process by performing regular inspections at various stages of manufacturing. Ensure that manufacturing processes comply with established quality standards, and identify any deviations or potential issues early in the production cycle. Work closely with the production team to maintain consistent product quality and resolve any quality-related issues that arise during manufacturing. Conduct testing and verification of products on the production line, ensuring they meet all design specifications. 5. Manufacturing Line Quality Control (QC): Oversee the quality control activities on the manufacturing line, ensuring that production outputs meet both internal and external quality standards. Conduct visual inspections, functional tests, and other quality assurance activities during production to prevent defects from reaching the final stages. Implement continuous improvement strategies to enhance product quality and reduce defects in the manufacturing process. Train production staff on quality control practices and ensure adherence to quality standards on the manufacturing line. 6. Outward Quality Control (QC): Conduct final inspections on finished products before they are dispatched to customers or the next stage of the supply chain. Ensure that all outgoing products meet the required quality specifications, including dimensions, functionality, and packaging. Perform random sampling or full inspections of products in compliance with the company’s quality standards. Document and report any defects or issues identified during outward quality inspections and work with relevant teams to address them before dispatch. 7. Vendor Management and Certification: Ensure that all vendors and suppliers are certified and meet the quality standards required by the company. Regularly review vendor performance based on quality metrics, and conduct audits to assess their compliance with contractual and quality requirements. Work with the procurement team to assess potential new suppliers, ensuring that they meet the company's quality criteria before being approved. Maintain vendor certification records and ensure that any issues related to vendor quality are addressed in a timely manner. 8. Documentation and Reporting: Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all quality control activities, including inspection results, quality alerts, corrective and preventive actions, and vendor performance. Prepare and present regular quality control reports to management, providing insights into product quality, issues, and actions taken. Ensure proper documentation of non-conformance reports (NCRs), inspection reports, and CAPA records for audits and internal reviews. 9. Continuous Improvement and Quality Enhancement: Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the overall quality management system. Suggest and implement strategies for improving product quality, reducing waste, and optimizing production efficiency. Monitor quality performance trends and propose initiatives for improving processes based on data-driven insights. 10. Training and Development: Conduct training sessions for production and quality control teams on quality standards, procedures, and best practices. Ensure that all personnel involved in quality control are well-versed in quality processes, tools, and techniques to maintain high-quality outputs. Keep up to date with the latest industry trends, standards, and best practices in quality control to continuously improve processes. Train employees on the product and manufacturing process as needed. 11. Compliance and Regulatory Requirements: Ensure that all quality control activities are in compliance with relevant regulations, industry standards, and company policies. Regularly review and stay updated on regulatory changes that may impact product quality or quality control processes. Assist in audits (both internal and external) related to quality control, ensuring that the company’s practices align with regulatory requirements. 12. Ad-Hoc Responsibilities: Provide support on quality-related projects or assignments as needed, including product development, process optimization, or new vendor evaluations. Address any immediate quality control concerns or issues raised by production, customers, or vendors. Take on additional quality control responsibilities assigned by senior management to support the company’s objectives. Qualifications and Skills: Bachelor’s degree in Quality Control, Engineering, or related field. Proven experience in quality control or quality assurance in manufacturing, preferably in a water purification or similar industry. Strong knowledge of quality control processes, methodologies, and tools. Proficient in using quality control software and ERP systems. Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills. Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality standards. Job Types: Full-time, Permanent Pay: ₹23,000.00 - ₹27,000.00 per month Benefits: Health insurance Provident Fund Ability to commute/relocate: Kavundampalayam, Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu: Reliably commute or planning to relocate before starting work (Required) Application Question(s): What is your Current Salary (Per Month)? What is your Expected Salary (Per Month)? What is your Notice Period? Experience: Quality control: 2 years (Required) Work Location: In person

title: Quality Control Engineer
description: 1. Inward Quality Control (QC): Inspect and evaluate raw materials, components, and products received from vendors to ensure they meet company specifications and quality standards. Conduct thorough testing and analysis of incoming materials to identify defects, inconsistencies, or deviations from quality requirements. Document findings from inward quality inspections and coordinate with the procurement team to resolve any quality issues with suppliers. Maintain a record of inspection results and report any non-conformance to management for corrective actions. 2. Quality Alerts and Communication: Issue quality alerts when defects or quality issues are identified during the inspection process. Ensure that quality alerts are communicated promptly to the relevant teams, including production, procurement, and vendors. Follow up on the implementation of corrective measures resulting from quality alerts and ensure timely resolution of identified issues. Maintain a log of quality alerts to track recurring issues and their resolution status. 3. Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA): Implement corrective actions for any identified non-conformance or quality issues, ensuring that root causes are effectively addressed. Develop and monitor preventive actions to avoid the recurrence of similar issues, ensuring long-term improvements in the quality system. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to investigate the causes of quality defects and implement solutions that align with company goals. Document all corrective and preventive actions taken and evaluate their effectiveness over time. 4. In-Process Quality Control (IP QC): Monitor and control quality throughout the production process by performing regular inspections at various stages of manufacturing. Ensure that manufacturing processes comply with established quality standards, and identify any deviations or potential issues early in the production cycle. Work closely with the production team to maintain consistent product quality and resolve any quality-related issues that arise during manufacturing. Conduct testing and verification of products on the production line, ensuring they meet all design specifications. 5. Manufacturing Line Quality Control (QC): Oversee the quality control activities on the manufacturing line, ensuring that production outputs meet both internal and external quality standards. Conduct visual inspections, functional tests, and other quality assurance activities during production to prevent defects from reaching the final stages. Implement continuous improvement strategies to enhance product quality and reduce defects in the manufacturing process. Train production staff on quality control practices and ensure adherence to quality standards on the manufacturing line. 6. Outward Quality Control (QC): Conduct final inspections on finished products before they are dispatched to customers or the next stage of the supply chain. Ensure that all outgoing products meet the required quality specifications, including dimensions, functionality, and packaging. Perform random sampling or full inspections of products in compliance with the company’s quality standards. Document and report any defects or issues identified during outward quality inspections and work with relevant teams to address them before dispatch. 7. Vendor Management and Certification: Ensure that all vendors and suppliers are certified and meet the quality standards required by the company. Regularly review vendor performance based on quality metrics, and conduct audits to assess their compliance with contractual and quality requirements. Work with the procurement team to assess potential new suppliers, ensuring that they meet the company's quality criteria before being approved. Maintain vendor certification records and ensure that any issues related to vendor quality are addressed in a timely manner. 8. Documentation and Reporting: Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all quality control activities, including inspection results, quality alerts, corrective and preventive actions, and vendor performance. Prepare and present regular quality control reports to management, providing insights into product quality, issues, and actions taken. Ensure proper documentation of non-conformance reports (NCRs), inspection reports, and CAPA records for audits and internal reviews. 9. Continuous Improvement and Quality Enhancement: Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the overall quality management system. Suggest and implement strategies for improving product quality, reducing waste, and optimizing production efficiency. Monitor quality performance trends and propose initiatives for improving processes based on data-driven insights. 10. Training and Development: Conduct training sessions for production and quality control teams on quality standards, procedures, and best practices. Ensure that all personnel involved in quality control are well-versed in quality processes, tools, and techniques to maintain high-quality outputs. Keep up to date with the latest industry trends, standards, and best practices in quality control to continuously improve processes. Train employees on the product and manufacturing process as needed. 11. Compliance and Regulatory Requirements: Ensure that all quality control activities are in compliance with relevant regulations, industry standards, and company policies. Regularly review and stay updated on regulatory changes that may impact product quality or quality control processes. Assist in audits (both internal and external) related to quality control, ensuring that the company’s practices align with regulatory requirements. 12. Ad-Hoc Responsibilities: Provide support on quality-related projects or assignments as needed, including product development, process optimization, or new vendor evaluations. Address any immediate quality control concerns or issues raised by production, customers, or vendors. Take on additional quality control responsibilities assigned by senior management to support the company’s objectives. Qualifications and Skills: Bachelor’s degree in Quality Control, Engineering, or related field. Proven experience in quality control or quality assurance in manufacturing, preferably in a water purification or similar industry. Strong knowledge of quality control processes, methodologies, and tools. Proficient in using quality control software and ERP systems. Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills. Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality standards. title: Workstation Engineer
description: Join a global Contract Resource Organization (CRO) where innovation meets purpose. At Worldwide Clinical Trials , we're driven by a shared commitment to improving lives through high-quality clinical research. Our teams are empowered to think creatively, take ownership, and deliver meaningful work that helps bring life-changing therapies to patients around the world. With more than 4,000 professionals across the globe, we foster a collaborative and inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are valued, growth is encouraged, and every contribution makes an impact. Whether you're building your career or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to learn, grow, and help shape the future of clinical research. SUMMARY: The Workstation Engineer is responsible for the design, lifecycle management, security, standardization, and continuous improvement of Worldwide's end-user computing environment. This role ensures that employee devices, operating systems, endpoint management platforms, and productivity tools remain secure, reliable, compliant, and aligned with business needs. The Workstation Engineer evaluates emerging technologies, maintains endpoint technology roadmaps, manages hardware and software standards, validates compatibility, administers endpoint management solutions, and supports the deployment of secure workstation technologies across a global enterprise environment. The role works closely with Security, Infrastructure, Service Desk, Procurement, and business stakeholders to deliver a modern digital workplace experience. Industry best practices emphasize endpoint lifecycle management, modern device management, cloud-managed endpoints, automation, and Zero Trust security principles. RESPONSIBILITIE S Tasks may include but are not limited to Endpoint Strategy & Roadmap Own and maintain the global workstation hardware roadmap. Define and manage approved standards for laptops, desktops, monitors, docking stations, peripherals, and mobile computing devices. Develop lifecycle and refresh strategies for end-user hardware. Recommend future-state endpoint solutions aligned with business, security, and operational requirements. Collaborate with Procurement and vendors to evaluate new hardware platforms and technologies. Technology Evaluation & Innovation Research, evaluate, and assess new endpoint technologies, operating systems, management tools, and productivity solutions. Conduct proofs of concept (POCs) and pilot programs for emerging technologies. Evaluate compatibility, supportability, security risks, and operational impact of new solutions. Provide recommendations based on technical, business, security, and user experience considerations. Hardware & Software Compatibility Testing Design, coordinate, and execute testing activities for workstation hardware, operating systems, drivers, applications, and peripherals. Validate compatibility between business applications and supported endpoint platforms. Develop testing standards, procedures, and acceptance criteria. Document findings and support enterprise-wide deployment decisions. Endpoint Engineering & Administration Engineer, deploy, and maintain Windows and macOS workstation environments. Manage endpoint configuration standards and images. Configure and support endpoint management platforms such as Microsoft Intune, Autopilot, Jamf, and related technologies. Develop automation and self-service solutions to improve endpoint management and user experience. Create and maintain endpoint configuration, compliance, and security policies. Patch & Vulnerability Management Test, validate, and deploy operating system, driver, firmware, and application updates. Assess software patches for potential business impact prior to enterprise deployment. Develop deployment schedules and rollout strategies. Monitor patch compliance and remediation activities. Partner with Cybersecurity teams to address endpoint vulnerabilities and reduce risk exposure. Security & Compliance Support Zero Trust and endpoint security initiatives. Ensure workstation configurations comply with organizational security standards and regulatory requirements. Partner with Security teams to implement endpoint protection, encryption, device compliance, and conditional access controls. Participate in security reviews, audits, and compliance assessments. Operational Support Serve as Tier 3 escalation support for complex workstation-related incidents and problems. Perform root cause analysis and drive permanent corrective actions. Engage vendors and manufacturers to resolve product defects and technical issues. Support major incidents impacting endpoint services. Documentation & Process Improvement Develop and maintain technical standards, procedures, runbooks, and knowledge articles. Maintain endpoint architecture documentation and hardware standards catalogs. Continuously improve workstation deployment, support, and lifecycle processes. Identify opportunities for automation and operational efficiency. Project Participation Lead or participate in endpoint modernization initiatives. Support workstation-related workstreams for mergers, acquisitions, office openings, and technology refresh projects. Collaborate with Infrastructure, Cloud, Networking, Cybersecurity, and Service Desk teams to deliver endpoint solutions. OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES: Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills. Technology evaluation and decision-making. Project and change management. Process improvement mindset. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to balance security, usability, and operational requirements. Vendor management and stakeholder engagement. Documentation and knowledge management. Customer-focused approach. Ability to work independently in a global environment. Success Measures The Workstation Engineer will be measured on: Endpoint compliance and security posture. Hardware roadmap effectiveness and lifecycle management. Patch compliance and vulnerability remediation performance. Device reliability and user experience metrics. Reduction in endpoint-related incidents. Successful delivery of endpoint modernization initiatives. Automation and operational efficiency improvements. Quality of documentation and technical standards. REQUIREMENTS: Education Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field. Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered. Experience 5+ years of experience in endpoint engineering, workstation engineering, desktop engineering, or end-user computing. Experience managing enterprise-scale Windows workstation environments. Experience with endpoint lifecycle management and hardware standardization. Experience testing and validating hardware and software compatibility. Experience managing software deployment and patch management processes. Technical Skills Windows 10/11 administration and engineering. Microsoft Intune and Endpoint Manager. Windows Autopilot. Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). Microsoft 365 platform. PowerShell scripting and automation. Endpoint security technologies. Software packaging and deployment. Hardware lifecycle and asset management. Driver and firmware management. Device compliance and configuration management. Remote support and endpoint troubleshooting. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting macOS environments. Experience with Jamf Pro. Experience with Azure Virtual Desktop or other virtual desktop technologies. Experience with Tanium or similar endpoint management platforms. Experience with Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX/DEM) tools. ITIL Foundation certification. Microsoft Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate. Microsoft Certified: Modern Desktop Administrator (or successor certification). Experience operating within a regulated environment such as healthcare, clinical research, pharmaceutical, or life sciences industries. Promotion to the next level is not automatic based on years of experience. Personnel are evaluated on proven competency, level of responsibility, and ability to work independently. Discover the Difference We love knowing that someone is going to have a better life because of the work we do. Discover the Difference at Worldwide Clinical Trials. Explore additional opportunities on our careers page, visit http://www.worldwide.com/careers , or connect with us on LinkedIn .

From our hands-on, accessible leaders, to our cohesive and supportive teams, we are committed to enabling professionals from all backgrounds and experiences to succeed.

title: Senior Systems Virtualization Engineer
description: Job Title: Systems Virtualization Engineer Experience: 10+ Years Work Mode: Remote Location: Remote Employment Type: Full-Time Company Overview Nuventure Connect is an ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 certified technology services company that leverages deep technology expertise to solve complex business problems and empower clients worldwide. Our commitment to state-of-the-art solutions spans the entire product value chain, delivering next-generation software, end-to-end IoT solutions, cloud infrastructure management, and managed IT support services. About the Role Nuventure Connect is looking for an experienced and highly motivated Virtualization Engineer to join our Engineering team. In this role, you will be responsible for designing, deploying, managing, securing, and optimizing enterprise virtualization platforms across multiple customer environments. The ideal candidate will have strong expertise in VMware technologies, enterprise backup solutions, storage infrastructure, virtualization lifecycle management, disaster recovery, and infrastructure troubleshooting. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver reliable, secure, and scalable virtualization services while maintaining high operational standards. Key Responsibilities Design, implement, document, maintain, secure, and continuously improve virtualization infrastructure across multiple sites and customer environments. Administer VMware vSphere and related virtualization platforms, including clusters, hosts, virtual machines, templates, host profiles, vMotion, resource allocation, lifecycle management, and platform licensing. Install, configure, test, patch, upgrade, and maintain operating systems, platform software, and systems management tools in accordance with approved standards and change-control processes. Monitor platform health, performance, capacity, and availability; identify trends and remediate risks before they affect customers or service commitments. Provide Tier 2 and Tier 3 support for escalated incidents, service requests, problems, and projects involving managed infrastructure and technologies; perform root-cause analysis and drive issues through resolution. Design and execute migration and onboarding strategies for customer workloads and internal platforms, including discovery, dependency validation, testing, cutover, rollback planning, and post-migration stabilization. Evaluate and implement storage, backup, replication, and disaster-recovery solutions aligned with customer requirements, recovery objectives, security controls, and operational standards. Collaborate professionally with customers, vendors, Engineering, Support, Network, Security, and leadership to design, implement, and support reliable services. Develop and maintain accurate architecture diagrams, standards, runbooks, knowledge articles, configuration records, ticket updates, and shift-handoff documentation. Provide technical leadership, coaching, and knowledge transfer to colleagues on virtualization technologies, operational practices, and troubleshooting methods. Meet assigned service, quality, project, and operational performance objectives; maintain relevant technical knowledge and certifications; and participate in the Engineering team’s rotating on-call schedule within a standard 40-hour workweek. Required Education and Experience Five or more years of professional experience administering complex, multi-site enterprise VMware environments, including vSphere clusters, ESXi hosts, vCenter, host profiles, templates and customization, vMotion, deployment, configuration, upgrades, and ongoing maintenance. Hands-on experience building, deploying, supporting, and maintaining virtual machines and the underlying compute, storage, and network integrations. Practical experience administering multi-tenant Veeam environments, including Veeam Backup & Replication, Veeam Cloud Connect, backup and restore operations, monitoring, troubleshooting, and recovery validation. Experience supporting data protection, replication, or recovery technologies such as Zerto and OpenText, or comparable enterprise platforms. Working knowledge of enterprise storage technologies, including NAS, SAN, and iSCSI, and their integration with virtualized environments. Working knowledge of core networking concepts, including VLANs, firewalls, load balancers, NAT, DNS, and LAN/WAN connectivity. Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex infrastructure issues methodically, assess risk, exercise sound judgment, and communicate technical findings clearly. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create operational documentation and work effectively with customers and cross-functional teams in a remote environment. Proven ability to organize and prioritize concurrent operational issues, escalations, and project commitments while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines. Preferred Skills Administration of additional virtualization or cloud platforms, including Proxmox VE, Microsoft Hyper-V, or Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization. VMware Horizon or hosted desktop-as-a-service environments. VMware NSX-T or comparable software-defined networking technologies; legacy NSX-V experience is also valuable. Technical leadership of virtualization, storage, migration, or infrastructure modernization projects. Hyperconverged infrastructure technologies and enterprise capacity planning. Infrastructure security, hardening, vulnerability remediation, backup immutability, and recovery testing. Experience supporting multiple customer environments within a managed services provider. Desired Competencies Veeam Certified Engineer (VMCE) or equivalent advanced Veeam certification. VMware Certified Professional, Data Center Virtualization (VCP-DCV), or higher. ITIL Foundation or higher. Alignment with Nuventure Values At Nuventure, how we work is as important as what we deliver. Team members are expected to demonstrate Nuventure's core values: Customer Focus: Place customers at the center of decisions and service delivery. Will-Do Attitude: Approach challenges with initiative, accountability, and a focus on creating customer value. Collaboration: Work responsively and constructively with others toward shared outcomes. Core Competencies Customer focus and professional service delivery. Ownership and accountability from initial identification through verified resolution. Analytical thinking, disciplined troubleshooting, and practical problem-solving. Attention to detail, sound organization, and consistent follow-through. Calm, clear communication during complex incidents and customer-impacting events. Collaboration, receptiveness to direction and feedback, and willingness to share knowledge. Continuous learning and adaptability as platforms, standards, and business requirements evolve.
